stories.title: Iran claims strike on US radar in Bahrain; US says it downed two Iranian drones
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike on a telecom tower in southern Iran, while US Central Command said it shot down two Iranian attack drones and reported no damage or injuries. The exchange heightens tension in the Gulf amid a fragile lull in the US-Iran war.

stories.title: Bus-truck collision in India's Assam kills at least 24
stories.summary: At least 24 people were killed and 11 injured when a container truck collided head-on with a bus near Kaziranga National Park in Assam, northeast India, police said. It is among the deadliest road accidents in the region this year.

stories.title: Zelenskyy announces largest-ever Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv and Moscow have agreed to the war's largest prisoner-of-war exchange, calling it a 'real result' of negotiations with US envoys. European representatives are set to join the next round of peace talks.

stories.title: Microsoft 365 outage: services recovering after ~18 hours, 'not cyber or AI'
stories.summary: Microsoft said it 'addressed the underlying issue' behind a global outage of Outlook, Teams and Copilot that disrupted users in at least 70 countries, blaming a network capacity upgrade rather than a cyberattack or AI agents. Services began recovering Friday after roughly 18 hours.

stories.title: Anthropic Claude hit by authentication outage across web and code tools
stories.summary: Anthropic's Claude.ai, Claude Code and platform console suffered elevated authentication errors starting around 09:58 UTC Friday, with users reporting login loops and hung sessions before services recovered about two hours later. The incident came as Microsoft separately worked through its own outage.

stories.title: Monken: Browns won't change struggling offensive line
stories.summary: Despite allowing an NFL-high 38 sacks and having two tackles with the league's worst pressure rates, Todd Monken said he is not planning any offensive line changes. The unit faces another test as Deshaun Watson returns with his deeper dropbacks.

stories.title: Denzel Boston questionable for Week 10 vs Texans; Hickman, Burton ruled out
stories.summary: Rookie WR Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable for Sunday against Houston after returning to Friday practice as a limited participant, while FB Michael Burton (calf) and S Ronnie Hickman (concussion) were ruled out. Boston's toe is 'trending in the right direction,' Todd Monken said.

stories.title: Jared Verse addresses sackless season, says he met with team psychiatrist
stories.summary: Edge rusher Jared Verse, who has no sacks through nine games, said he sought help from the team's sports psychiatrist to work through what he called a 'mental block.' Verse was acquired in the offseason trade that sent Myles Garrett to the Rams.

stories.title: Deshaun Watson returns as Browns starter against Texans
stories.summary: Todd Monken said Deshaun Watson will reclaim the starting quarterback job against Houston after clearing concussion protocol, citing his 'full body of work' over the first eight games. Second-year QB Shedeur Sanders filled in during a Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints.

stories.title: Justyn Martin still pushing for a chance in Ohio State's QB room
stories.summary: Fifth-year transfer Justyn Martin remains the third-string quarterback behind Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair but says he prepares 'like he's one snap away.' Martin is weighing whether to use a sixth year of eligibility at Ohio State in 2027.

stories.title: Buckeyes 'desperate for a win' heading into Northwestern
stories.summary: After consecutive losses dropped Ohio State to 6-3, Ryan Day said the team is 'desperate for a win' and must beat Northwestern at home Saturday. Center Carson Hinzman said the team has to rally around freshman QB Luke Fahey.

stories.title: Ohio State fires special teams coordinator Robby Discher after nine games
stories.summary: Ryan Day fired special teams coordinator Robby Discher — his first in-season assistant firing — after costly errors swung losses to USC and Oregon. Senior analyst Rob Keys will oversee special teams by committee for the rest of the season.

stories.title: Brandon Inniss cleared for Northwestern; Luke Montgomery questionable
stories.summary: Receiver Brandon Inniss was cleared to play Saturday against Northwestern, but offensive lineman Luke Montgomery is questionable, keeping the injury bug alive on a struggling O-line. Quarterback Aidan Chiles is out for the Wildcats.

stories.title: Daily Mail boycotts F1 coverage after FIA revokes journalist's accreditation
stories.summary: The Daily Mail said it will boycott Formula 1 coverage for the final three races after the FIA revoked correspondent Jonathan McEvoy's accreditation over a column critical of Charles Leclerc. McEvoy called the move an attack on press freedom.

stories.title: Yuki Tsunoda risks losing Monza point as FIA sets appeal hearing
stories.summary: The FIA confirmed Audi's appeal over Yuki Tsunoda's Monza restart will be heard November 25, more than two months after the Italian GP. If the appeal succeeds, Tsunoda could lose the point for tenth place, which would go to Gabriel Bortoleto.

stories.title: Former Liberty Media CEO: F1 could be taken private by 2028 in $30B deal
stories.summary: Greg Maffei predicted Formula 1's public-market era could end within two years in a deal valuing the series near $30 billion. He suggested the opportunity to cash out is imminent as EBITDA growth stabilizes.

stories.title: Toto Wolff: Mercedes CEO rejected his repeated resignation offers
stories.summary: Toto Wolff revealed at the Golden Steering Wheel awards that he offered to resign multiple times during Mercedes' recent performance slump, but CEO Ola Kallenius refused each time. Wolff said the backing convinced him to stay and rebuild.

stories.title: Escape from Tarkov director: console version to be announced in 2027
stories.summary: Battlestate Games director Nikita Buyanov said a console version of Escape from Tarkov will be announced next year '100%,' though it won't be ready in 2027. The studio is still seeking a publishing partner and has yet to add controller support on PC.

stories.title: Hilliard teacher resigns after allegations of inappropriate relationship with student
stories.summary: A teacher at Hilliard's Ryan Griesmer Memorial Middle School resigned amid allegations of an inappropriate relationship with a student, with the district, police and the state education board reviewing the case. The matter remains under investigation.

stories.title: Netflix's 'KPOP DEMON HUNTERS' live show coming to Schottenstein Center
stories.summary: Netflix and AEG Presents will bring the HUNTR/X live concert experience based on the animated 'KPOP DEMON HUNTERS' to Columbus's Schottenstein Center next summer, part of a wave of arena events landing in the city.

stories.title: Giving Machine arrives at Polaris to support people in need
stories.summary: A 'Giving Machine' — a red vending machine that lets shoppers donate specific items to local charities — opened at Polaris Fashion Place on Friday as part of a holiday-season giving push connecting shoppers with nonprofit needs.

stories.title: Ohio nurses plan complaints against OSU Wexner Medical Center over staffing
stories.summary: The Ohio Nurses Association said it will file state complaints against Ohio State's Wexner Medical Center CEO and The James' chief nursing officer, alleging staffing shortages contributed to canceled open-heart surgeries and ICU bed closures.
